name: hazard_lab
title: Too dangerous for school (virtual lab)
summary: Explosions, molten iron and a hydrogen fireball, watched from arm's length. None of this is allowed in a real school; in VR nobody can get hurt.
banner: Explosions, fire and molten metal here cannot hurt anyone. Never try any of this in real life.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Welcome to the hazard lab. Today: experiments no real school would ever let you watch from this close.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: First, alkali metals in water. The teacher writes the reaction: the metal makes hydrogen gas.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Lithium goes in first. It floats and fizzes gently: those bubbles are hydrogen.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Sodium melts into a shiny ball and catches fire with a yellow-orange flame, spitting sparks.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Potassium bursts into a lilac flame at once, and sparks fly out of the trough.

steps.speaker: student_2
steps.caption: Next is caesium, which explodes. A student asks: is it safe to stand this close? In VR, yes.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: BANG! The caesium explodes. The trough shatters and water sprays all over the bench.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Broken glass and water everywhere, and nobody hurt. In a real lab this is done behind blast shields.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Next, thermite: rust and aluminium powder. It burns at about 2500 degrees C.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: The powder sits in a clay pot above a steel plate. The teacher lights the magnesium fuse.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: It ignites: blinding white light, a fountain of sparks and white smoke.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: White-hot molten iron pours out of the bottom of the pot onto the steel plate.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: It burned straight through the steel plate. The iron lump in the sand is still glowing red.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Last one: hydrogen burning in air. The teacher writes the reaction in red.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: A balloon full of hydrogen. A flame on a long pole creeps up underneath it.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: WHOOMP! A fireball: the hydrogen burns with the oxygen in the air in a split second.

steps.speaker: instructor
steps.caption: Nobody was hurt and nothing needs cleaning up: in VR we can repeat it as often as we like. Press R to watch again.
